item.title: Safer at Height: Why Arborists Are Trading Ropes for Spider Lifts
item.description: Before the school bell, a tree team rolls a compact tracked spider into a narrow side passage, lays a run of ground mats and brings a dead ash gently down over a glass atrium. No climber suspended above the footpath, minimal noise, no surprises for neighbours. It is a picture of how urban tree work increasingly gets done. The post Safer at Height: Why Arborists Are Trading Ropes for Spider Lifts appeared first on The London Economic.
